headline: Georgie Prespakis wins AFLW best and fairest award
summary: Georgie Prespakis secured the AFLW’s top individual honour after a tight final round count, edging out rival Garner who broke the All-Australian selection record. The award recognises the league’s best player for the season.

headline: Ackman warns US recession risk if Fed hikes rates
summary: Hedge-fund manager Bill Ackman said on X that the United States could slip into recession if the Federal Reserve raises interest rates, arguing that financial conditions are already significantly tighter.

headline: Nvidia shares rise after Trump push to reinstate CEO
summary: Nvidia stock bounced higher on Monday following reports that the Trump administration is urging the reinstatement of founder Jensen Huang as chief executive, adding to a weekend of positive developments for the chipmaker.

headline: Capita shares tumble as chief resigns amid pension saga
summary: Shares in public-sector outsourcing group Capita fell sharply after its chief executive stepped down, with the decline linked to ongoing delays in civil-service pension payments overseen by the firm.

headline: Chamonix mayor proposes tourist caps to protect Alpine area
summary: The mayor of Chamonix announced plans to limit visitor numbers at Lac Blanc after a surge in hikers and cable-car users has strained the environment and diminished the experience, with daily summer arrivals now exceeding 4,000.

headline: NHS caterer Compass eyes primary listing move to New York
summary: UK health-care catering giant Compass is reportedly planning to shift its primary stock exchange listing from London to New York, a move that would join a series of recent relocations and could impact the FTSE 100’s composition.

headline: UK AI datacentre rollout lifts manufacturing, housebuilder shares slump
summary: The rollout of AI-driven datacentres is boosting UK manufacturing output, while housebuilder Crest Nicholson warned of a profit shortfall, sending its shares down more than a quarter and dragging peers such as Barratt Developments and Persimmon lower.

headline: Spain’s far-right Vox surges towards 20% vote share
summary: Spain’s Vox party, which received just 0.2% of the vote in 2016, is now on track for almost 20% in the upcoming election, positioning it as a potential coalition partner in a future government.

headline: Teen on trial for e-motorbike death of nurse
summary: A teenager is facing a manslaughter trial after allegedly striking and killing a nurse while riding an electric motorbike, with the case now before the courts.

headline: Tories welcome Haigh’s hint at Natural England abolition
summary: UK Conservative MPs praised First Secretary of State Louise Haigh’s suggestion that the government could adopt the party’s plan to scrap Natural England, part of a broader quango-reduction agenda.

headline: Penny Wong warns of new era of global coercion
summary: Foreign Minister Penny Wong, in a landmark speech, cautioned that the world is entering a period where international rules are eroding, urging Australia to adapt to heightened US-China rivalry and cooperate with allies to safeguard national interests.

headline: Anthropic and Nvidia shares climb in pre-market trading
summary: Shares of AI start-up Anthropic and chipmaker Nvidia rose in early trading after a broad tech sell-off, as the Nasdaq recorded its worst week since early 2020 with a 10% decline.

headline: South East Water posts £22.9 m pre-tax loss
summary: The UK water utility reported a pre-tax loss of £22.9 million for the six months to 30 September, citing supply issues.

headline: US Treasury yields rise as stock futures rebound
summary: U.S. Treasury yields jumped on Monday, partially reversing last week’s declines, while stock futures pointed to a strong Wall Street rebound ahead of New York Fed President Williams’ speech.

headline: Sergey Brin lists Malibu estate for $33.5 m
summary: Google co-founder Sergey Brin and ex-wife Nicole Shanahan have put their Malibu home on the market with an asking price of $33.5 million.

summary: A sharp increase in mortgage rates in September has deepened the slowdown in the real estate sector, tightening conditions for buyers, sellers and the broader economy.

headline: Musicians pay tribute to TV music legend Ian Meldrum
summary: Kylie Minogue, Jimmy Barnes and other Australian artists have publicly honoured late music champion Ian ‘Molly’ Meldrum, praising his influence on the industry and recalling his iconic role on national television following his recent death.

headline: Teen injured after metal pole hurled through car windscreen in Brisbane
summary: A 19-year-old man was taken to hospital after a metal pole was thrown at his vehicle on a busy inner-Brisbane road, breaking the windscreen and striking him, police said.

headline: NAB email error reveals staff redundancies ahead of official notice
summary: National Australia Bank sent an automated email on Monday morning that mistakenly informed employees their system access would be terminated next week, inadvertently confirming upcoming layoffs before the formal announcement.

headline: French biotech Abivax shares tumble 17% after short-seller allegations
summary: Abivax faced a 17% plunge in its share price after short-seller Scorpion Capital accused the company of scientific and safety flaws in its experimental inflammatory bowel disease drug, which the firm has denied.

headline: Morgan Stanley strategist sees buying opportunity amid market capitulation
summary: Morgan Stanley’s lead strategist argues that low Nasdaq valuations, declining earnings expectations and a sharp drop in investor sentiment create a favourable entry point for investors, describing the current market environment as a “fat pitch”.

headline: UK minister calls for overhaul of disability benefit assessments
summary: Disability Minister Sir Stephen Timms announced plans to recommend sweeping reforms to the Personal Independence Payment system, saying the current assessment process needs a fundamental overhaul.

headline: Two convicted over failed tonne-scale cocaine import into Western Australia
summary: A court found two people guilty of roles in a botched attempt to bring nearly a tonne of cocaine into Western Australia, describing the plot as an embarrassment to organised crime, while two others were acquitted.

headline: Zelenskyy says Ukraine sank Russian warship in Libya
summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy claimed Kyiv was responsible for the sinking of the Russian warship Merkury in Benghazi, Libya, and praised the drone operation that achieved the strike, amid reports of a separate drone attack on a Russian cargo vessel in the Baltic Sea.

headline: France’s street protests: who is on the streets and why
summary: Reporters outline the composition of demonstrators in recent French protests, noting President Macron’s attribution of unrest to the radical left and detailing the various groups and grievances driving the rallies.

headline: Queensland mother on trial for murder of six-month-old son
summary: A trial began in Queensland for a mother accused of murdering her six-month-old son, with prosecutors presenting evidence while the defence seeks to challenge the charges.

summary: The S&P/ASX 200 has fallen about 8% from its August high but lost only half as much as the Nasdaq, suggesting the Australian market may be better positioned than its US counterpart.

headline: Australian data-centre sector faces leadership shake-up and expansion plans
summary: NextDC’s outgoing chairman Doug Flynn is under scrutiny after the company’s M3 delays, while Nasdaq-listed Iren has purchased a former South Australian school to house staff for a $10 billion data-centre project. A CFMEU witness also took a prominent role in a regulator inquiry, highlighting industry turbulence.

headline: Kenya and DR Congo restore diplomatic relations after conflict-related tensions
summary: Leaders of Kenya and the Democratic Republic of Congo pledged to uphold sovereignty and non-interference, agreeing to re-establish diplomatic ties that had been strained by recent conflict issues.

summary: European gas prices surged on Monday as a forecast cold snap raised concerns over an already depleted winter supply. The Dutch month-ahead benchmark rose up to 8.6% to €96.08 before settling 4% higher at €92.50, reflecting worries about higher household bills.

summary: Former Australian captain Steve Smith made a brief return to Sheffield Shield cricket for New South Wales but was dismissed cheaply after a neck injury, falling early in the match against Queensland.

summary: The prime minister will tell MPs that the EU agreement reached on Friday offers a choice between a broken status quo or change, describing the deal as a landmark that could improve the next decade.

summary: Analysis shows that rapid, steep declines in the S&P 500 have been followed by a rebound 91% of the time over the past decade, prompting traders to weigh whether the current correction signals a reversal or further weakness.

summary: Police declared a major incident after a substance, believed to be tear gas, was released into the crowd during a performance by US rapper Don Toliver in Manchester, prompting evacuation of the venue.

headline: Sydney suburb ranked last in A-to-Z guide for ‘swampy and poor’ homes
summary: An A-to-Z guide of Sydney suburbs places a once-industrial area, now home to a thriving multicultural community, at the bottom of the list, describing its homes as "swampy and poor".

headline: Kim Jong-un declines meeting with Trump during Asian tour
summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong-un did not meet US President Donald Trump during the latter’s Asian tour, marking another missed opportunity for the two leaders to engage on nuclear and diplomatic issues.

headline: NSW Labor campaign material draws criticism as party’s popularity falls
summary: As polls show a slide in Prime Minister Albanese’s popularity, NSW Labor’s advertising material has attracted internal criticism, with some campaign assets leaning heavily on Premier Chris Minns to bolster the party’s image.

headline: Manly Sea Eagles hire former All Blacks coach to staff
summary: Manly Sea Eagles football director Steve Hansen has secured a former All Blacks and Wallabies coach to join Kieran Foran’s staff at Brookvale, describing the recruit as the best skills coach available.

summary: A One Nation candidate for Williamstown has promoted conspiracy theories about vaccines and delivered anti-Muslim remarks, even threatening to fight a civil war over the issues, despite party backing.

headline: Over 1 million Jetstar customers may join class action over Covid-era refunds
summary: More than 1 million Jetstar passengers could be eligible for a class action alleging the airline failed to provide cash refunds for flights cancelled between 2020 and late 2022, after a federal court ordered notices to be sent to customers.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese dismissed critics as “jumping at shadows”, sparking a political dispute over ministerial powers.

summary: Negotiations reveal Beach Energy is buying into the Taroom Trough gas project while Santos looks to offload its stake, highlighting differing strategies in Queensland’s emerging oil and gas province.

headline: Asian regulators act to steady markets as AI-related chip slump deepens
summary: Regulators across Asia are introducing measures to support sagging equity markets, focusing on chipmakers and hardware suppliers most exposed to the recent downturn in AI-related trading activity.

headline: Australian buyer moves to Wales’s cheapest town amid local housing strain
summary: A property hunter swapped an Australian home for a house in Wales’s most affordable town, where rising investor interest is clashing with locals’ ability to afford homes.

summary: Drilling at Lewis Ponds in New South Wales has intersected three mineralised zones, extending Orbit Resources’ known gold-silver-base metal resource beyond its previously defined 17.52-million-tonne model.

headline: Socceroos debutant Eli Adams faces year-long injury lay-off
summary: Eli Adams, who made his Socceroos debut, has been ruled out for up to twelve months after sustaining a serious injury shortly after his first international appearance.

headline: Woman on trial for murder after failing to protect infant from abusive father
summary: The prosecution alleges that baby Rhuan suffered severe injuries, including a fractured skull, at his home in Yugar, leading to a murder trial for the mother who is accused of neglect.

summary: The South Australian government’s PACE program awarded Red Metal Ltd a $350,000 grant to explore a large copper-gold deposit close to BHP’s Carrapateena mine.

summary: Chalmers told parliament the government is on track to fund spending cuts ahead of the mid-year budget update, while forecasts point to higher unemployment and slower growth.

summary: Private-wealth firm Walker Lane has withdrawn from its insurance operations as part of a broader consolidation trend affecting smaller players in the sector.

summary: Federal investigators are examining Megaspeed and its associate Alice Huang after reports linked a former associate to deep involvement in activities related to the Nvidia chip investigation.

summary: Research finds that a common sales pitch used by shops and restaurants increases the effectiveness of traps for catching black rats.

summary: Police say thousands of recent 000 calls were for non-urgent matters such as cold food and ingrown toenails, prompting a campaign to reduce unnecessary emergency calls.

summary: The crocodile-wrangling celebrity admitted failing to maintain his helicopters, exposing pilots and passengers to serious risk of injury or death.

The Oxfam and Conflict and Environment Observatory study warns the poisoned water, soil and air could affect generations.

summary: Geoff Henke, credited with building Australia’s winter-sports programme after his own Olympic disappointment, passed away at 99. His efforts helped generations of Australian athletes compete at the Winter Games, earning him the reputation of a ‘dream maker’ in the sport.

summary: Iran-aligned Houthi rebels said they carried out an operation against Saudi Arabia’s Rabigh oil refinery. The claim comes as diplomatic attempts to end the Yemen war stall, raising concerns about further disruptions to regional oil supplies.

summary: Forrestania Resources has started wet commissioning at its Edna May gold mine in Western Australia, feeding the first ore into the crusher. The company aims to produce its inaugural gold pour by December, marking a key milestone for the project.

summary: Auric Mining has accelerated the dismantling of its $1.2 million processing plant, planning to move the equipment to Burbanks by December. The move is a critical step toward establishing the company as an independent gold producer in Western Australia.

summary: Cricket New South Wales refused permission for the Perth-based NRL expansion side, the Bears, to play a trial match at the historic North Sydney Oval, effectively ending the club’s hopes of a homecoming at the venue.

summary: Footage of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents detaining a father and daughter on an Alaska Airlines boarding bridge went viral, prompting protests at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport and condemnation from local officials who called the tactics un-American.

summary: Sydney Swans players Isaac Heeney, Chad Warner, Riley Bice and James Jordon returned to official pre-season training on Monday following clearance from recent criminal conduct allegations.

headline: Body recovered from Yarra after two men jump from Princes Bridge
summary: Police retrieved a man's body from the Yarra River on the day after two men were seen jumping into the waterway from Princes Bridge, prompting a police investigation.

headline: Beau Lamarre-Condon double-murder trial enters closing stage
summary: The double-murder trial of former NSW police officer Beau Lamarre-Condon moved into its final days as the defence barrister delivered a closing address and the jury prepared to deliberate.

summary: The Perth Bulls secured a high-profile signing, marking their biggest market move, while the PNG national team’s upcoming target participated in a golf outing with the Australian prime minister.

headline: Iron Bear lifts Canadian iron ore project valuation to US$11.6bn
summary: Iron Bear Resources raised the post-tax valuation of its Canadian iron ore project by 29% to US$11.6 billion after cutting capital costs and increasing planned annual production, highlighting a significant upside for the asset.

headline: Western Australia to criminalise coercive control
summary: Premier Roger Cook announced plans to introduce legislation making coercive control a criminal offence from next year, aiming to strengthen protections against family and domestic violence in the state.

summary: Gateway Mining reported a one-metre interval with 16.5 grams per tonne gold at its Panakin prospect in Western Australia’s Yandal belt and is now drilling the discovery at depth with a diamond rig.

summary: Unrelated trading halts at Canaccord and Maas Group on Monday morning drew attention from market participants, prompting speculation and discussion across the Australian share market.

headline: Brisbane family home sells for $1.3 million after nine-way bid
summary: A five-bedroom house in Brisbane defied the broader market slowdown, achieving a $1.3 million sale price at auction following a competitive nine-way bidding war.

headline: Alex Greenwich withdraws request for Fred Nile state funeral
summary: After public backlash, MP Alex Greenwich has retracted his earlier request for a state funeral for the late Reverend Fred Nile, known for his opposition to same-sex marriage and Mardi Gras protests.

headline: Perth Bears coach Meninga comments on staff turnover
summary: Perth Bears head coach Mal Meninga described the club’s early staff turnover as chaotic, noting the recent dismissal of chief executive Anthony De Ceglie among other departures.

headline: RBA modelling suggests CGT changes could lift inflation
summary: Reserve Bank of Australia modelling indicates that proposed capital gains tax reforms may add upward pressure to inflation, prompting concerns among policymakers.

summary: Critics argue the AFL draft no longer serves as an equalisation tool, citing academy, father-son and free-agent selections that favour stronger clubs.

headline: Lendlease rules out emergency capital raising
summary: Lendlease said it will not pursue an emergency equity raise despite lingering debt concerns and recent valuation drops of more than $2 billion.

headline: Glencore float on ASX may spur more dual listings
summary: Bankers say Glencore’s recent ASX listing could encourage other overseas miners to pursue dual listings as the exchange reforms to attract foreign resources companies.

headline: NSW Labor MPs report voter anger over Albanese economy
summary: State Labor members say they are hearing widespread frustration from constituents about Prime Minister Anthony Albanese’s handling of the economy ahead of the next election.

headline: Investor snaps up four Clovelly homes for $6 million
summary: A buyer employed a smart bidding strategy to acquire four properties in Clovelly, paying a total of $6 million amid a low overall auction clearance rate.

summary: Australia’s Wallabies enjoyed a win in Wales, but coach Les Kiss now faces his toughest selection week ahead of the Ireland test, with strong performances from substitutes complicating his squad choices.

summary: Premier Chris Carroll warned that the state was “too slow on crime” in a campaign speech, saying the upcoming election is the one he was made for, as Labor faces a likely wipe-out.

summary: Drone attacks on Sudan’s capital have killed at least four civilians and injured nine, with reports also indicating damage to a United Nations building in Khartoum.

summary: A former elite soldier faces a rape trial after a jury heard he argued the woman gave “advanced consent” by snoring, despite her being incapacitated and motionless in the video evidence.

summary: Former US president Donald Trump will headline his third cryptocurrency gala at his Virginia golf club, rewarding holders of his meme coin, as Democrats allege he is profiting from the venture.

summary: M&A activity is heating up, and investors are urging ASX-listed companies, such as IDP, to actively engage with prospective buyers, intensifying scrutiny on board responsiveness.

summary: Discount retailer Poundland has been given a matter of days to secure a buyer, otherwise it may be forced into administration, raising concerns about its future viability.

summary: After releasing ten psych-rock albums, Perth-based group Pond has reinvented its sound, adopting a darker, gothic-inspired style for pub performances while continuing to critique Western Australian culture through their lyrics and stage presence.

summary: Advertising campaigns are increasingly using the claim that ageing alters body odour to promote expensive soaps, tapping into social-media-driven shame and nostalgia to drive sales among older consumers.

summary: Star centre-fielder Latrell Mitchell is caught in a back-room power struggle at the Rabbitohs, with reports of factional infighting threatening team cohesion as the club navigates a turbulent season.

summary: Former captain Pat Cummins is praised for helping restore Australia’s cricket ethos after a period of decline, though analysts warn the sport now faces fresh challenges that could test his legacy.

summary: Residents of Barnham, Suffolk, held a symbolic referendum on whether to separate from the United Kingdom after the government proposed housing 930 asylum seekers at a nearby former military base, with 257 of 274 votes supporting the split.

summary: President Donald Trump signed an executive order requiring federal contractors and subcontractors to seek White House approval before responding to any congressional requests, warning that non-compliance could jeopardise their contracts.

summary: Financial advisers discuss the pros and cons for retirees with two superannuation accounts contemplating a shift to pension mode, highlighting factors such as tax implications, income stability and long-term investment strategy.

summary: Mercedes-Benz plans to introduce its Drive Assist Pro update, enabling automated short-range urban trips, to Australian drivers within 18 months, marking a significant step toward wider adoption of autonomous vehicle technology down under.

headline: Retail magnate Gerry Harvey reinvests in sandalwood oil venture
summary: Gerry Harvey, founder of Harvey Norman, has bought back a stake in his sandalwood oil side business, citing growing consumer demand for wellness products as the driver behind the renewed investment.

summary: A leaked webinar from a notorious Australian cult reveals a scheme that harvested millions of dollars from terminally ill followers. The operation targeted vulnerable cancer patients, extracting life savings under the guise of spiritual guidance.

headline: Trump meets Albanese as US-Australia ties shift
summary: US President Donald Trump hosted Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, signalling a warmer relationship. Observers note the Australian leader is adapting to evolving US diplomatic rules, highlighting the nuanced dynamics of the bilateral partnership.

summary: The lavish revamp of Cabra-Vale Diggers Club into a Vegas-style resort has drawn scrutiny for alleged cost overruns, targeted dismissals, dubious contract variations and clashes among senior executives, raising questions about governance and financial oversight.

headline: Mexican authorities capture drug cartel boss ‘El Chapo Isidro’
summary: Mexican special forces raided Sinaloa, arresting Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as “El Chapo Isidro”, a top FBI-wanted drug trafficker. He was seized with two alleged gang leaders after a gun battle that sparked panic in Guasave.

headline: Australians find cheaper homes and jobs in Berlin
summary: Three Australians moved to Berlin seeking lower living costs and better opportunities. They report cheaper housing and larger prospects, though some aspects of Australian life are harder to leave behind.

headline: US Vice-President Vance stops short of backing Trump’s Iran claim
summary: At a White House briefing, Vice-President JD Vance declined to endorse President Trump’s assertion that Iran was on the brink of acquiring a nuclear weapon, saying it was not his place to second-guess the president.

headline: Amazon nears $7.5bn acquisition of AI start-up Decart
summary: Amazon’s cloud unit AWS is close to finalising a purchase of AI start-up Decart for about $7.5 billion, a move aimed at strengthening its position against Nvidia in the high-performance computing market.

headline: Trump says FBI hack could have a positive spin
summary: Former US president Donald Trump suggested the recent intrusion into the FBI’s database might yield a "positive spin" for him, marking the second known breach of the agency’s systems in recent weeks.

headline: UN talks on autonomous weapons collapse after Russian opposition
summary: Negotiations at the UN Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons in Geneva failed to secure a mandate for a legally binding treaty on autonomous weapons, with Russian objections preventing agreement and the conference adopting a weaker option.

headline: Virginia records first measles-related death of 2026
summary: A child under four years old died in Virginia, marking the state’s first measles-associated fatality of the year and adding to a US outbreak that recently cost the country its measles-elimination status.

headline: British father recalls despair after son’s death in Cyprus
summary: A British man sentenced to a €3,000 fine for his two-year-old son’s fatal fall from a fourth-floor hotel window in Cyprus described the moment of panic and loss of control, recalling the despair he felt as the child slipped from his grasp.

headline: Tech outages spur concerns over AI cyber-attacks and power grid
summary: Recent technology outages have heightened worries about AI-driven cyber-attacks and the vulnerability of the U.S. electricity grid, prompting analysts to warn of a growing “doomsday economy” as disruptions become more frequent.

headline: Perth burger joint ranks among world’s top ten
summary: A popular Western Australian burger chain, run by Alasdair and Ken Craigie, secured a place in the global top-ten list, becoming one of only two Australian eateries to feature alongside the iconic Fergburger.

headline: Top women in finance share practical investing tips
summary: Leading women in the U.S. finance sector offered straightforward investing advice, emphasizing that it’s never too late to start and highlighting strategies that can help individuals build and protect wealth.

headline: US judge refuses to release man shot by ICE agents
summary: A federal judge denied a request to release Oscar Belgal, a Dominican national wounded by ICE agents during an arrest in New York, ruling that a procedural error did not merit his release from custody.

headline: UK issues heavy rain warning for south-west England
summary: The Met Office issued a weather warning for south-west England as a slow-moving band of rain is expected to bring more than 100 mm of precipitation to Dartmoor, with flood alerts and power-cut risks highlighted.

headline: Princess of Wales discusses cancer journey in new BBC documentary
summary: Princess Catherine will appear in a forthcoming BBC documentary where she talks about her cancer diagnosis, the physical and emotional impact, and her participation in the Three Peaks challenge, offering a message of hope and resilience.

headline: Florida inmates describe extreme heat in prison leading to death
summary: In testimony, a 69-year-old inmate described sweltering conditions at Dade Correctional Institute, where concrete walls and temperatures above 119 °F contributed to a fellow prisoner’s death after he struggled to breathe.

headline: Retirees warned of RMD deadline to avoid tax penalty
summary: Financial advisers caution that missing the required minimum distribution deadline for retirement accounts during the busy holiday period could trigger a tax penalty for retirees.

headline: Mexico’s military captures FBI-most-wanted drug kingpin
summary: Mexican armed forces seized Meza Flores, a leader of the Beltrán Leyva gang and one of the FBI’s ten most-wanted fugitives, in a high-profile operation against the Sinaloa cartel’s rival factions.

headline: US USDA and FBI suffer cyber breaches amid tech outage concerns
summary: Hackers breached the US Department of Agriculture’s farmer-payment system and the FBI’s National Crime Information Center, raising alarms over a spate of recent technology outages at key American institutions. The intrusions were first reported by major US news outlets, with responsibility and links between the attacks still unclear.

headline: Anthropic AI IPO faces sharp sell-off as market correction bites
summary: Anthropic’s high-profile initial public offering initially surged but quickly fell as broader market correction pressures investors to reassess valuations of AI-focused stocks, prompting a notable sell-off on the day of the debut.

headline: California experiences modern-day gold rush
summary: Rising gold prices have sparked a new rush in California, with small-scale miners investing time and money to extract the precious metal, hoping to bring in millions from the booming market.

headline: Major US retailers roll out deep Thanksgiving meal-basket discounts
summary: Walmart, Target and Amazon are among the retailers advertising substantial Thanksgiving grocery bundles, offering lower-priced meal-basket deals as shoppers prepare for the holiday season.

headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s fortune could halve amid market doubts
summary: Analysts suggest that Nvidia founder Jensen Huang may see his net worth cut by up to 50 percent as the company’s valuation faces scrutiny and broader tech market corrections intensify.

headline: Zelensky calls strikes on Crimean Bridge a ‘fair response’
summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky described recent Russian aerial attacks on bridges, including the Crimean Bridge, as a fair response to Kyiv’s actions, speaking while meeting UK officials.

headline: Mexican drug lord on FBI’s most-wanted list killed in shoot-out
summary: Fausto Isidro “Chapo Idisro” Meza Flores, a Mexican drug trafficker and torture suspect listed on the FBI’s ten most-wanted, was captured after a gunfight with authorities.

headline: State and federal regulators clash over prediction-market rules after midterms
summary: Following the recent midterm elections, states, Congress and the CFTC are intensifying their dispute over how prediction markets should be regulated, with each side pushing differing legislative approaches.

headline: Warren Buffett quadruples Thanksgiving charitable gifts to $5.5 billion
summary: Billionaire investor Warren Buffett increased his Thanksgiving donations to four family foundations, raising the total to $5.5 billion, more than four times his previous contribution level.

headline: US Navy cost estimate for new Trump-class warships blows out by billions
summary: A report to Congress warned that the US Navy’s projected cost for the new Trump-class battleship fleet has risen by billions of dollars, with the acting secretary acknowledging strain from the Iran conflict.

headline: Reform UK eyes alliance with Restore Britain ahead of Castle Bromwich by-election
summary: Reform UK is considering a pact with hard-right party Restore Britain as both seek to improve poll performance ahead of the upcoming Castle Bromwich by-election in the West Midlands.

headline: Council urges residents to seek support as heating costs rise this winter
summary: A local council is advising households to access assistance programmes to cope with increasing energy bills for heating during the winter months.

headline: 6.8-magnitude quake rattles Northern Territory after East Timor tremor
summary: A 6.8-magnitude earthquake struck north-east of Lospalos in East Timor on Saturday, causing shaking across the Australian Top End. Residents in the Northern Territory reported rattling homes and buildings but no immediate reports of damage or injuries.

headline: Manchester sound-system groups revive reggae culture for youth
summary: The Megatone Sound Foundation and Baron Turbo Charge are using reggae sound-system events to give young Black Mancunians a sense of belonging and cultural education, sharing stories of community, work-life balance and heritage through music and large speaker stacks.

headline: Navy budget pick linked to contractor with Trump-family ties
summary: A recent US Navy procurement decision has drawn scrutiny after it was revealed that the selected contractor has family investments connected to a company linked to Donald Trump Jr., raising concerns about potential conflicts of interest.

headline: Traders shift US copper to China as tariff worries ease
summary: With Chinese copper shortages and a high local premium, traders are moving US copper shipments to China, exploiting arbitrage opportunities now that fears of renewed US tariffs on Chinese goods have subsided.

headline: US airlines launch mega business-class cabins as first-class ends
summary: Major US carriers are replacing traditional first-class cabins with expansive, luxury-focused business-class suites, offering passengers larger seats, private spaces and premium services in a bid to capture high-end demand.

headline: Lachlan Shaw grabs spectacular catch on debut for Australia
summary: In his first match for Australia, Lachlan Shaw dived to take a stunning outfield catch off Ben Dwarshuis’s delivery, earning praise for his reflexes and fielding skill.

headline: UK re-entry to EU on table as trade and youth deals signed
summary: British leaders say rejoining the European Union remains a possibility while formalising new trade and youth-mobility agreements with the bloc, following recent talks in Brussels.

headline: Parliamentary inquiry launched into online peptide clinics
summary: Health Minister Mark Butler has ordered a parliamentary investigation into telehealth operators and social media platforms promoting unapproved peptide drugs, amid concerns over a booming market for unregulated treatments.

headline: Black Friday liquid BBL deals face safety criticism in England
summary: Experts warn that seasonal promotions for liquid Brazilian butt lifts and other cosmetic procedures risk patient safety, citing the recent death of a woman after a botched liquid BBL and prompting a government consultation on restricting such treatments to qualified professionals.

headline: Haitians welcome El Salvador troops but fear escalation
summary: Many Haitians greet the arrival of El Salvador soldiers sent to combat entrenched gangs, while others worry the foreign offensive could worsen the volatile security situation that has plagued Port-au-Prince for years.

headline: Three teens charged over Perth shopping centre stabbing released on bail
summary: Police have charged three teenagers with an alleged stabbing at the Carousel Shopping Centre in Perth. All three have been released on bail as investigations continue.

headline: Olympic champion Jon Henricks dies at 91
summary: Jon Henricks, the Australian swimmer who won two gold medals at the 1956 Melbourne Olympics and set multiple world records, has died aged 91.

headline: FBI probes possible hack of criminal database
summary: The FBI is investigating an apparent intrusion into its National Crime Information Center database, which is used by federal and local law enforcement to share information. Authorities have not disclosed how the breach occurred or what data may have been accessed.

headline: Australia struggles to finalise climate deal centred on electrification
summary: Negotiators say Australia is seeking support for a climate agreement that focuses on electrification but omits references to fossil fuels. The lack of consensus on the fossil-fuel component is delaying the finalisation of the deal.

headline: Robber gives victim fist bump after supermarket robbery
summary: During a knife-point robbery at a Logan supermarket, the armed offender stole cash and then offered the victim a fist bump before fleeing. Police are investigating the unusual post-theft interaction.

headline: Cricket Australia confirms Cummins as Test captain
summary: Cricket Australia ended speculation by announcing that Pat Cummins has its unanimous support to lead the side in the first Test against New Zealand. The decision settles ongoing rumours about the captaincy.

headline: Proposed law could let Australians sue big tech firms
summary: A change to the Government’s digital duty of care legislation would allow Australians to bring legal action against major technology companies. The amendment aims to strengthen consumer protections online.

headline: Oslo cuts down 21-metre Christmas tree in Trafalgar Square
summary: The 21-metre tree, Norway’s annual thank-you gift to Britain for World War Two support, was felled in Trafalgar Square. The ceremony marks the start of the city’s Christmas celebrations.

headline: Lehmann apologises but denies knowledge of sandpaper plot
summary: Former Australian cricket coach Darren Lehmann issued an apology for his role in the 2018 sandpaper scandal but said he had no prior knowledge of the plan. The statement follows recent comments by former player Bancroft.

headline: Family keeps 4 am Christmas Eve carols tradition
summary: A family of carols enthusiasts forgoes last-minute shopping, instead queuing from 4 am on Christmas Eve to secure a prime spot for the Carols by Candlelight event, a ritual they say they cannot live without.

summary: Police have charged a 17-year-old identified as the online handle “Onepercent” for organising a series of firebomb attacks on Melbourne bars. He is accused of coordinating the arson offences and endangering public safety. The investigation remains ongoing.

summary: People living on South Australia’s Eyre Peninsula say recent power outages have left them uneasy. While work is under way to stabilise the regional grid, locals want stronger assurances that future blackouts will be avoided and energy security improved.

summary: Delegates from nearly 200 nations remain deadlocked at COP31 as disagreements over fossil fuel provisions prevent progress on a new global climate agreement.

headline: PM warned against dismissing top treasurer

summary: A global Ticketmaster system failure caused long queues and frustration for fans attending the AFLW preliminary final double-header at Ikon Park.

summary: Veteran racehorse Gringotts, ridden by Nash Rawiller, secured a third Gong victory, establishing a new record in the Big Dance series.

headline: Deutsche Bank warned of lasting impact of past decisions
summary: A Financial Times piece cautions Deutsche Bank executives that historical choices can have enduring consequences for the institution.

summary: Advocates urge a public debate on consent legislation after survivor Joanne Young highlighted gaps in the law regarding third-party consent and drug-facilitated rape.

summary: President Xi Jinping continues to use high-profile international summits as photo-op opportunities to broaden China's worldwide reach.

summary: A premature weakening of the polar vortex, combined with cold weather and low wind, could strain Europe's already low winter gas reserves.

summary: Common vulnerabilities are exposing ordinary businesses to cyber attacks, as AI tools enable criminals to operate more efficiently and swiftly.

headline: Kew inner-east townhouse sells for $2.11 million
summary: A mother secured a Kew townhouse opposite Studley Park with a strong bid, finalising the sale at $2.11 million.

headline: Man stabbed in Melbourne CBD, police say attackers unknown
summary: A 24-year-old man was attacked with a knife outside the H&M store on Bourke Street, Melbourne, and is in hospital fighting for his life. Police do not believe the two men involved knew each other.

headline: Nvidia co-founder accused of fostering hostile workplace culture
summary: Former and current employees allege Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang routinely humiliated staff, creating an environment described as terrorising and involving threats, insults and settlements.

headline: Netanyahu faces new parliamentary challenge four weeks after election
summary: Opposition parties have achieved a key parliamentary victory, intensifying the power struggle for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu as his tenure comes under renewed scrutiny.

summary: Kimi Antonelli secured pole position in qualifying but received a five-place grid penalty, handing Max Verstappen the top spot for the Las Vegas Grand Prix.

summary: A 15-year-old boy remains in hospital in critical condition after police say he was shot with an arrow in northern New South Wales.

summary: The North Melbourne Kangaroos defeated the Sydney Swans at Princes Park, securing a place in their fourth consecutive AFLW grand final.

headline: Kyiv residents remain unfazed by bridge damage after Russian missile strike
summary: Despite holes in the Northern Bridge caused by a Russian ballistic missile, Kyiv commuters continue using the remaining lane, showing confidence in the city’s infrastructure.

summary: Charity officials report a £200,000 drop in contributions after a barrier and €2 entry fee were implemented, reducing the number of tourists tossing coins into the fountain.

headline: Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo, Mexican drug lord, dies at 80
summary: Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo, known as “the godfather” of Mexico’s drug trade, passed away, leaving a legacy that reshaped the global narcotics industry through his extensive criminal network.

headline: Oil shipments through Hormuz decline as Iranian strikes rise
summary: Analysts say increased Iranian strikes are making Middle Eastern crude exports increasingly fragile, leading to a fall in oil shipped via the Hormuz Strait.

headline: CVC alleges accounting manipulation in €3bn Advent pastry deal
summary: Private-equity firm CVC claims the Advent-backed pastry ingredients transaction was overstated, while the US buyer denies the allegations.

summary: The Russia-Ukraine drone conflict has caused a six-times surge in the price of optical fibre, a key anti-jamming component. The spike threatens Kyiv’s drone communications and could ripple through global telecom supply chains.

summary: Construction firms across Europe are shifting focus to military projects, aiming to win contracts for bases, airports and bridges as the residential market weakens. The sector hopes the anticipated €620 billion defence spend will offset the slowdown in housing construction.

headline: Spirit of Tasmania ferry delayed again after technical issue
summary: The new Spirit IV ferry arrived in Geelong later than scheduled after spending hours looping in Port Phillip Bay and being escorted by a tug. This is the second late arrival this month, leaving passengers waiting for hours.

summary: Victoria police allege a 17-year-old used the encrypted app Signal to direct a group in a series of arsons, home invasions and a mistaken-identity kidnapping that left a victim with a partially amputated finger during Melbourne’s hospitality wars.

headline: Honda and Toyota recall 1.6 million US vehicles over airbag risk
summary: Honda and Toyota are recalling 1.6 million vehicles in the United States because of a risk that Takata airbag inflators could rupture. No injuries or crashes have been linked to the defect, which has caused deaths and injuries in past incidents.

summary: Political analysts say the Victorian Labor government is on track for a historic loss as Premier Ben Carroll and Opposition leader Jess Wilson campaign at early-voting centres ahead of the November 28 poll.

summary: A teenager is in critical condition after being stabbed with a large kitchen knife at a Sydney shopping centre, while another teen has been charged in connection with the attack.

summary: Former Rohingya refugees describe fleeing burning villages and rivers running red with blood, warning of the brutal tactics that forced them to abandon their homes in Myanmar.

summary: Analysts say the Nvidia affair has put China’s Ministry of State Security in the spotlight, underscoring worries about the scale and capability of Chinese cyber-espionage targeting Western technology firms.

summary: Authorities are probing the cause of a four-minute emergency-services outage in Canberra, including why the backup power system failed to activate during the incident.

summary: An 11-year-old died after being struck by a utility vehicle while crossing the South Western Highway near Kirup, a small town south of Perth.

headline: Accidental outback publican celebrates unexpected hotel ownership
summary: Stacy Henman reflects on the unlikely journey to owning the remote Tilpa Hotel after a nine-month process, sharing stories of the quirky characters that run the outback pub.

headline: Cricket Australia backs Cummins, drops Khawaja and Warner from commentary
summary: Fox Cricket has removed former captains Usman Khawaja and David Warner from its commentary team, while Cricket Australia gave Pat Cummins unequivocal support to remain captain. The decision follows internal reviews aimed at strengthening Cummins’ leadership.

headline: Two boys stabbed at Sydney shopping centre, teens charged
summary: Police charged a 17-year-old and arrested a 16-year-old after two boys were stabbed during an alleged confrontation at a north-west Sydney shopping centre. The victims said they were “lucky to be alive”, and the investigation continues.

headline: Bayer to pay $11 billion US settlement over Roundup cancer claims
summary: Bayer has agreed to an $11 billion settlement in the United States covering current and future non-Hodgkin lymphoma cases linked to its Roundup weed-killer. The deal resolves thousands of lawsuits alleging the product caused cancer.

headline: Dutch court bans BYD from selling copycat Land Rover in Europe
summary: A Dutch court has ordered Chinese EV maker BYD to stop selling its new 4x4 in Europe after finding the design too closely resembles Land Rover’s Defender. The ruling halts BYD’s planned European launch of the model.

headline: David Jones to cut around 1,700 jobs after Christmas
summary: The retail union says David Jones will dismiss nearly 1,700 staff following the holiday period. It will assist affected employees in finding new work and ensure the department store meets its financial commitments. The cuts reflect ongoing pressure on Australian retailers amid weak consumer spending.

headline: Four injured by lightning at NSW music festival
summary: Wild weather at the Strawberry Fields music festival in Tocumwal, New South Wales, resulted in four people being struck by lightning overnight. Emergency services attended the scene and provided medical care to the victims. Organisers warned of severe weather risks for future outdoor events.

headline: Rallies across Australia warn of freebirth rule impact
summary: Thousands gathered in towns and cities nationwide to protest new insurance regulations that could restrict midwife-supported homebirths. Protesters argue the rules will cause a “catastrophic collapse” in access to freebirths, urging the government to reconsider the policy to protect maternal choice and safety.

headline: Speculation mounts on AOC as potential US presidential candidate
summary: Following the recent US midterm elections, discussion has intensified about Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez possibly running for president. Commentators note her rising profile and the “bluenami” effect, suggesting she could become the first female president if she decides to launch a campaign ahead of 2028.

headline: AI surveillance technology detected in Australian university exams
summary: University staff say covert AI-driven surveillance tools have been used in exam rooms, raising concerns about student privacy and exam integrity. The technology can monitor movements and capture audio, prompting calls for stricter controls and clearer guidelines on the use of such systems in education.

headline: Underground ballet network emerges among young Iranian women
summary: Despite a long-standing ban on dance, a covert network of young Iranian women is organising secret ballet classes as an act of defiance. Participants risk arrest to practice the art, highlighting growing cultural resistance and the personal risks taken to preserve artistic expression.

headline: Kununurra faces rising youth crime, calls for more support services
summary: Community workers in the outback town of Kununurra say a surge in teenage crime is outpacing local resources. They urge state and federal authorities to provide targeted support, mentorship and structured programmes to address the underlying social issues driving the criminal behaviour.

headline: Liberal Party hopes to regain Kew as independent candidate runs
summary: In the Victorian electorate of Kew, a returning independent candidate is challenging the Liberal incumbent Jess Wilson. Party strategists believe Wilson’s high profile could help the Liberals win back voters in the traditionally safe seat ahead of the upcoming state election.

headline: Texas inmate claims pain during execution, officials deny botched procedure
summary: The Texas Department of Criminal Justice rejected allegations that the execution of inmate Reinaldo Dennes was mishandled after he reportedly screamed in pain. Officials maintain the protocol was followed correctly, despite the inmate’s claims of severe discomfort during the lethal injection.

headline: Schoolies week adds pickleball and line dancing to attract teens
summary: Gold Coast organisers of the annual Schoolies celebration introduced pickleball and line dancing to reflect changing teen preferences. Attendance remains strong but lower than previous years, prompting a shift towards more diverse, low-key activities as the traditional party scene evolves.

headline: Fraudsters fined $811 million for exploiting detained migrants
summary: A court ordered fraudsters to pay $811 million after they scammed detained migrants, running a bail-bond scheme that left many refugees in custody. Despite the fine, investigations reveal the illegal operations continued, prompting calls for tighter oversight of migrant-related financial services.

headline: Wall Street’s worst week in over a year creates buying opportunities
summary: Following the steepest market decline in more than a year, analysts say the sell-off has opened chances for investors to deploy cash, with many focusing on protecting portfolios rather than seeking new bargains.

headline: Consumer groups warn of scams during Black Friday and Cyber Monday
summary: Consumer watchdogs caution shoppers that many promotions over the Black Friday and Cyber Monday period may be misleading or fraudulent. They highlight common tactics such as fake discounts, hidden fees and deceptive pricing. Shoppers are urged to compare prices, read fine print and verify offers before purchasing to avoid falling victim to scams.

headline: Coroner to examine radicalisation of Perth teen killed by police
summary: A coroner will investigate whether a 16-year-old Perth teenager, who was shot by police after stabbing a stranger, could have been saved. The inquiry will consider the teen’s descent into radicalisation, from Marxist ideas to extremist behaviour, and assess factors that may have contributed to the fatal incident.

headline: ANC struggles to retain control of South African metros after election loss
summary: South Africa’s African National Congress faces challenges keeping authority over key metropolitan areas following setbacks in recent elections. The party appears reluctant to adopt a power-sharing arrangement with the pro-business Democratic Alliance at the local level, raising concerns about governance and service delivery in major cities.

headline: Victorian Greens seek court injunction over misleading how-to-vote cards
summary: The Victorian Greens have applied to the Supreme Court for an urgent injunction to stop independent candidate Tosh-Jake Finnigan from distributing how-to-vote cards that mimic the party’s branding and advise voters to preference the Greens last. The Greens argue the cards could confuse voters and unfairly benefit the Liberal Party.

headline: Trump frames White House press briefing as succession test
summary: During a press conference, President Donald Trump put senior officials Jeff Vance and Marco Rubio under scrutiny as potential successors, while Stephen Miller unexpectedly dominated the discussion. The event was described as a rehearsal for the 2028 presidential succession, with Trump posing pointed questions about future leadership.

headline: AI models tested on Black Friday TV deal hunting
summary: Four artificial-intelligence models were evaluated by the BBC to see if they could identify cheaper Black Friday television offers. The trial examined the potential for AI to help consumers save money during the sales period.

headline: Australia’s Holstein steer Tiny Tim may set national size record
summary: Tiny Tim, a Holstein-Friesian steer standing over 190 cm tall, is being touted as the biggest living steer in Australia, potentially surpassing the previous record holder Knickers.

headline: California holds vigil honouring civil-rights icon Dolores Huerta
summary: Hundreds gathered in Bakersfield for a celebration-of-life event for Dolores Huerta, co-founder of the United Farm Workers. Speakers highlighted her legacy and the widespread tributes across the state following her passing.

headline: New York mayor announces plan to close Rikers Island jail by 2032
summary: Mayor Eric Adams confirmed a timeline to shut down the Rikers Island jail complex by 2032, continuing a plan first approved in 2019. The closure will require relocation of inmates to alternative facilities.

headline: Man found guilty of igniting 2025 Palisades fire in Los Angeles
summary: Jonathan Rinderknecht was convicted at his second trial for starting the 2025 Palisades fire in Los Angeles, a blaze that killed 12 people and caused extensive damage.

headline: A Beautiful Noise touted as next big musical after Hamilton
summary: The new musical starring Will Swenson as Neil Diamond, A Beautiful Noise, is being promoted as a must-see show, with praise for Swenson’s vocal resemblance to Diamond.

summary: BBC reports that the US Army postponed the controlled explosion of unstable lead azide in eastern Iowa after residents and lawmakers raised worries about a potentially toxic plume from the blast.

summary: Florida executed a man convicted of murdering a pregnant woman and her husband, marking the state's 20th execution this year, while Texas also carried out a death sentence.

summary: Sean Cairncross was dismissed as the White House national cyber director following a series of technology outages that affected US air travel, banking and national security, with DoD CIO Kirsten Davies stepping in temporarily.

headline: South Australian woman convicted of murdering parents with insulin
summary: A South Australian jury found a woman guilty of killing her parents by administering insulin, concluding a five-month murder trial.

headline: Melbourne teacher pleads guilty to hidden camera offence
summary: Timothy Blamires, a 33-year-old teacher, admitted to installing a hidden camera in the male toilets at Kingswood Primary School after being reported by a cleaner.

headline: Virgin Australia in talks with Boeing and Airbus for fleet expansion
summary: Virgin Australia is negotiating with Boeing and Airbus as it looks to order additional aircraft to expand and modernise its fleet.

headline: SBS wins Walkley award for teen radicalisation documentary
summary: SBS was awarded a Walkley in the Current Affairs short category for its documentary on teen radicalisation, marking the second win for The Feed team after their 2023 victory.

summary: Rising fuel costs and tough economic conditions have pushed 85% of Australian vegetable growers to consider exiting the industry within a year, raising concerns over national food security.

headline: New novel explores extreme thinness obsession
summary: Catherine Chidgey’s latest novel follows a young woman forced into a sideshow act where she must not eat for 40 days, highlighting society’s fixation on thinness.

headline: Mother receives suspended sentence for crash killing 6-year-old
summary: A judge described a mother who caused a fatal crash that killed her six-year-old daughter in Adelaide’s north as a "good person" who made a terrible mistake, handing down a suspended sentence.

headline: Future of $600m Maryvale waste incinerator in doubt after grant cut
summary: The federal government quietly terminated a grant for the Maryvale waste-to-energy incinerator in Victoria’s Latrobe Valley, casting uncertainty over the $600 million project’s future.

headline: Rio Tinto pledges $370m to Bougainville landowners
summary: Rio Tinto announced a $370 million commitment to address environmental and social impacts in Bougainville, a move welcomed by local landowners who said they felt overwhelmed by the pledge.

headline: NRL releases 2027 season draw and grand-final rematch plan
summary: The National Rugby League unveiled the schedule for the 2027 season, featuring marquee match-ups and outlining a lengthy wait for a grand-final rematch.

headline: Black-market peptide trade fuels Australian health-boost trend
summary: A surge in Australians using untested peptide injections for weight loss, muscle gain and longevity is being driven by both legal and illegal channels, according to recent reporting.

headline: Data challenges Greta Thunberg’s climate criticism of Australia
summary: Ten charts reveal a more nuanced picture of Australia’s climate performance, countering claims that the nation is moving at a snail’s pace on emissions reductions.

headline: Chalmers warns of spending hitting 40% of GDP
summary: Treasurer Jim Chalmers said Australia’s spending is set to reach 40% of GDP as a decade of deficits pushes the economy beyond capacity, fuelling inflation and prompting multiple cash-rate hikes.

headline: Builders accused of slowing Sydney-airport metro project
summary: Contractors working on the 23-kilometre rail link to Western Sydney International Airport have been accused of a go-slow, delaying the line’s opening beyond the start of passenger flights.

headline: De Minaur leads star-studded field in Australian Open warm-up
summary: Australian No 1 Alex de Minaur will headline a highly competitive Australian Open tune-up event, featuring a line-up described as the strongest ever for a home tournament. The match-play will give players a chance to fine-tune form ahead of the Grand Slam.

headline: Sydney councils seek limits on e-bike numbers and parking
summary: Local councils in Sydney are proposing new powers to curb e-bike usage, including caps on fleet sizes, penalties for improper parking and an age restriction for riders. The measures aim to address safety and congestion concerns on city streets.

headline: African nations urge Europe to honour pledged climate finance
summary: At the UN climate summit in Turkey, African delegations pressed European countries to deliver on previously pledged climate-finance commitments, arguing that existing funds are insufficient to cope with the continent’s escalating climate impacts.

headline: Albanese’s overseas trips bring diplomatic wins but domestic criticism
summary: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese’s recent foreign visits have secured progress on Quad defence drills, fuel security and high-level China engagement, yet have sparked domestic backlash over fast-food outings and summit spending, highlighting a split between international gains and home-front discontent.

headline: Judge rules USDA religious emails breach First Amendment
summary: A federal judge found that messages sent by U.S. Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins to agency staff, which included Christian prayers and imagery, violated the Constitution’s separation of church and state, ordering her to avoid proselytising in official communications.

headline: Elderly man dies in Launceston suburban grass fire
summary: An elderly resident of Launceston succumbed to injuries after a grass fire broke out in his neighbourhood. Police thanked community members who attempted to assist the man before emergency services arrived.

headline: Exmouth cyclone recovery hampered as new season begins
summary: Residents of Exmouth, Western Australia, still repairing damage from the previous cyclone season, expressed concern that the onset of a new season could further delay recovery efforts and strain already stretched resources.

headline: US warns nuclear-sub supply to Australia could cut its own fleet
summary: A report to the U.S. Congress cautioned that providing nuclear-powered submarines to Australia under the Aukus pact would reduce the U.S. Navy’s own submarine numbers for many years and raised questions about obligating Australian vessels to U.S. conflicts.

headline: Lenders seek safeguards to block SpaceX chip-launch financing
summary: Investors financing a $40 billion semiconductor programme are demanding legal protections to prevent SpaceX from using the launch to transport chips into orbit, aiming to secure collateral and limit exposure to space-related risks.

headline: Canada attracts AI data-centre investment as US opposition grows
summary: Canada is becoming a hub for AI data-centre projects, drawing interest from investors like Kevin O’Leary, while similar initiatives in the United States face local resistance, highlighting divergent policy environments for high-performance computing infrastructure.

headline: Residents describe daily life under siege in Yemen's Taiz
summary: People trapped in the Houthi-controlled city of Taiz say they live amid constant shelling, shortages of food and water and limited electricity. Families speak of fear and uncertainty as the conflict continues to isolate the city from the rest of Yemen.

headline: Airbnb introduces new house rules for hosts and guests
summary: Airbnb has rolled out new rules that limit what hosts can ask guests to do, aiming to reduce chores for visitors. The changes may increase costs for customers while standardising expectations across listings.

headline: New pill shows promise against pancreatic cancer
summary: Early trial results of the oral drug daraxonrasib indicate it can shrink or even eliminate tumours in some patients with pancreatic cancer, offering hope for a disease with poor survival rates.

headline: GLP-1 weight-loss drugs prompt food-industry menu changes
summary: The arrival of the first GLP-1 weight-loss tablets in Australia is leading chefs, supermarkets and fast-food chains to rethink portion sizes and menu offerings as consumers adjust eating habits.

headline: UK launches nationwide operation to secure thousands of fridges from hackers
summary: A secret operation in the United Kingdom has secured tens of thousands of commercial refrigerators in supermarkets, warehouses, restaurants and stadiums after a wave of cyber threats targeting the devices.

headline: Sydney man charged after Islamic State material seized in raids
summary: Police arrested a Sydney man following counter-terrorism raids on several properties, discovering material linked to the Islamic State. The suspect now faces charges related to terrorism offences.

headline: Gap appoints new Athleta CEO, cuts guidance
summary: CNBC says Gap has named Ashley Kechter as the new chief executive of its Athleta brand and lowered its full-year financial guidance following mixed third-quarter earnings.

headline: Anthropic IPO sees shares rise 17% but fails to lift tech sector
summary: Anthropic's highly anticipated IPO opened with a 17% share price jump, yet technology stocks overall fell and the broader sector did not receive a lift, leaving investors questioning the AI rally.

headline: Trump posthumously pardons baseball legend Pete Rose
summary: BBC notes that former US President Donald Trump issued a posthumous pardon for Pete Rose, the baseball icon who died in 2024 after a lifetime ban for betting on games was lifted the previous year.

headline: US sanctions target Australian Comanchero gang over drug links
summary: The United States has imposed sanctions on the Comanchero organised crime group, marking the first time an Australia-based gang has been hit by such measures due to alleged drug-trafficking connections.

headline: Watchdog urges removal of religion from Australia’s terrorism law
summary: The Independent National Security Legislation Monitor recommended deleting references to religion from Australia’s terrorism definition, arguing they foster discrimination and give false legitimacy to extremist narratives, and called for reforms to the nation’s counter-terrorism statutes.

headline: Analysts dismiss Trump-Xi-Putin summit as empty rhetoric
summary: Commentators argue that the peace declaration from the recent summit between Trump, Xi and Putin lacked substance and failed to address the complex issues facing global relations.

headline: Cumin-flavoured sodas gain ground in India
summary: Cumin-infused fizzy drinks are winning market share from major cola brands in India as consumers gravitate towards locally inspired flavours. The trend highlights shifting taste preferences and presents a challenge for multinational beverage makers seeking to retain dominance in the market.

headline: Australian U-17 side beats Argentina 2-0 in Qatar
summary: Sydney FC prodigy Akol Akon starred as the Joeys secured a surprise 2-0 victory over Argentina to open their under-17 World Cup campaign in Qatar. The win showcased emerging Australian talent and raised hopes for a strong tournament performance.

headline: Bowen removes fossil-fuel language from COP31 text
summary: Australian Energy Minister Chris Bowen succeeded in stripping all references to fossil fuels from the draft UN climate agreement at COP31, pushing instead for a new global electrification target. The move signals a shift toward clean-energy language in international climate negotiations.

headline: Cybersecurity stocks rise as S&P 500 falls
summary: Amid a broad decline across all 11 S&P 500 sectors, cybersecurity shares were the only group to post gains on Thursday. The sector’s resilience highlighted investor confidence in continued demand for digital security solutions despite market weakness.

headline: California AG subpoenas Nvidia in China chip probe
summary: The California Attorney General issued a subpoena to Nvidia as part of an investigation into the diversion of AI chips to China. The probe follows the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and reflects heightened scrutiny of semiconductor exports to the Chinese market.

headline: Treasury doubts Woollahra’s 9,400-home target
summary: Internal Treasury advice warned that the NSW government’s plan to deliver 9,400 new homes in Woollahra is unrealistic due to high land and construction costs. Labor’s housing pledge faces scrutiny as affordability concerns mount.

headline: Thomas Markle deemed fit for trial
summary: A court-appointed psychiatrist found Prince Harry’s father, Thomas Markle, mentally competent to stand trial on child-abuse charges. The ruling clears a procedural hurdle ahead of the upcoming legal proceedings.

headline: One Nation warns as ex-NSW opposition leader quits
summary: Former NSW opposition leader Mark Speakman announced his departure from politics, marking the eighth Liberal MP to resign ahead of the upcoming election. One Nation seized on the exit to highlight perceived instability within the coalition.

headline: ElectraNet to investigate tower collapse on Eyre Peninsula
summary: South Australian Premier announced an independent inquiry into the failure of a transmission line tower that caused power outages on the Eyre Peninsula. Officials hope the investigation will enable restoration of electricity later today.

headline: US Congress passes Financial Exploitation Prevention Act
summary: Both chambers of the US Congress approved the Financial Exploitation Prevention Act of 2025, aimed at protecting older investors from financial fraud and strengthening safeguards against abusive schemes.

headline: Blackpool sacks manager Ian Evatt hours after birthday wish
summary: English club Blackpool dismissed manager Ian Evatt on the same day it posted a birthday greeting to him on social media, ending his tenure abruptly.

headline: Queensland man charged with murder of three-month-old daughter
summary: A Queensland man has been charged with domestic-violence murder after his three-month-old daughter, who was taken to Logan Hospital with serious injuries, died the following day.

headline: Paralympian Liesl Tesch to compete in third sport at 2026 World Championships
summary: 57-year-old Liesl Tesch, already a star in basketball and water sports, will represent Australia in para ice hockey at the 2026 Women’s World Championships in Newcastle.

headline: CEOs propose three priorities for new Victorian government
summary: Top executives from NAB, REA and Bunnings have outlined three key actions they believe the incoming Victorian administration should take after the November 28 election. Their recommendations focus on infrastructure, housing affordability and boosting the state’s economic competitiveness.

headline: Market signals point to recession concerns despite solid data
summary: Analysts note an increase in recession-focused trades even as recent economic data remains broadly supportive, raising worries about the economy’s near-term trajectory.

headline: Firmus downplays Tasmanian data centre economic impact
summary: Firmus seeks to have its proposed Tasmanian data centre assessed under normal planning rules, describing the project’s economic benefits as modest after earlier claims of a $46 billion boost.

summary: AARP and other experts argue that Senator Ron Johnson’s description of Social Security as a “legal Ponzi scheme” mischaracterises the program, which faces a trust-fund shortfall but operates under different principles.

headline: UnitedHealth shares tumble amid Medicare fraud crackdown fears
summary: UnitedHealth’s stock fell 19% over five days as regulators signal tighter audits of Medicare Advantage ‘upcoding’ and new Medicare-for-All proposals, prompting a slide in other health-insurance equities.

headline: European leaders say united stance for Ukraine talks in Berlin
summary: EU allies of Ukraine claim they have a united negotiating position ahead of a summit in Berlin aimed at ending the war with Russia.

headline: US Commerce clears over 879,000 AI chips for Chinese firms
summary: The Commerce Department approved sales of more than 879,000 artificial-intelligence chips to Chinese companies, prompting congressional calls for tighter export controls after the Jensen Huang scandal.

headline: Considerations for granting a spouse enduring power of attorney
summary: While safeguards exist to prevent abuse, giving a spouse authority over financial affairs remains a matter of trust, according to advice on enduring powers of attorney.

headline: Intuit to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for $3.68 billion
summary: Intuit announced the sale of its Mailchimp division to Bending Spoons for $3.68 billion, a price less than a third of the amount paid for the acquisition in 2021, citing slowed revenue growth.

summary: AMD fell more than 7% following a short-seller report claiming its firmware appeared in a blacklisted Chinese firm; the company said it complies with U.S. law.

headline: Walmart expands focus on fast-food delivery
summary: Walmart says roughly 90% of fast-food spending occurs within a few kilometres of its stores, prompting a larger investment in delivery services.

headline: Drink-spiking reports rise at Northern Territory sexual assault centre
summary: The NT Sexual Assault Referral Centre records at least one drink-spiking report every fortnight, highlighting ongoing concerns about safety in the region.

headline: Fiona the hippo dies after swallowing knitted hat
summary: Cincinnati Zoo’s famous hippo Fiona died after attempts to remove a knitted hat she swallowed proved unsuccessful, despite various medical interventions.

headline: Adelaide motorists warned of road closures for Supercars event
summary: Temporary closures on South Road will begin Friday for the Adelaide Grand Final Supercars weekend and continue for two weeks, causing major traffic disruptions.

summary: Palo Alto Networks posted better-than-expected first-quarter results and announced a $4.5 billion agreement to acquire AI startup Applied Compute, boosting its AI-focused strategy.

headline: Australian PM Albanese to meet Xi amid iron-ore tensions
summary: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese will hold bilateral talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping, with the meeting set against a backdrop of rising tensions over Australian iron-ore exports.

headline: UK and EU near reset deal as summit approaches
summary: British and European negotiators are close to a reset agreement, provisionally allowing 100,000 EU citizens to work in the UK each year and dropping a demand for EU students to pay home tuition fees. The deal is expected to be finalised at the upcoming summit.

headline: Karis Davidson tops first round of LPGA Tour Championship
summary: Australian golfer Karis Davidson seized the clubhouse lead after the first round of the LPGA Tour Championship in Florida, defying expectations and marking a strong start for the prestigious event.

headline: Amazon warns New York of higher costs if delivery law passes
summary: Amazon has warned that New York City could face higher delivery costs if the proposed Mamdani delivery legislation is enacted, after lobbying heavily against the bill supported by the mayor.

headline: Pat Cummins’ captaincy under scrutiny amid Sandpapergate fallout

headline: Law firms that worked with Trump face new congressional scrutiny
summary: U.S. law firms that provided services to former President Donald Trump are hiring external counsel as Democrats begin probing the deals made during his administration.

headline: Kraken parent Payward acquires venture firm Tribe Capital
summary: Payward, the owner of crypto exchange Kraken, announced the purchase of venture capital and asset-management firm Tribe Capital, marking a move into private-market investing for the exchange group.

headline: CoreWeave co-founder bets $30 million on company bonds
summary: Brian Venturo, co-founder of AI-focused cloud provider CoreWeave, purchased $30 million of the firm's distressed bonds, signalling confidence amid broader AI sector jitters.

headline: US Senate rejects war powers resolution targeting Iran conflict
summary: The Senate voted 48-51 to defeat a resolution that would have forced the president to halt military action against Iran, with Republican senators defending the ongoing conflict.

headline: Nvidia shares tumble as market cap loss tops $600 billion
summary: Nvidia's stock fell sharply, wiping out roughly $611 billion in market value over six trading days, prompting concerns about the chipmaker's role as a de-facto AI central bank.

headline: Australian minister downplays recession fears amid job cuts
summary: Minister Amanda Rishworth dismissed economist warnings of a recession as Australian firms announced further job reductions.

headline: Consumer watchdog urged to act on burn injury from Temu hoodie
summary: Following a severe burn suffered from a recalled Temu hoodie, the victim's family and former ACCC head Allan Fels are calling for the regulator to intervene despite limited legal recourse.

headline: S&P 500 heads for sixth consecutive decline
summary: The US S&P 500 index is on track for a sixth straight day of losses, while Johnson & Johnson reported progress on two key product launches.

summary: Caitlin Foord received the Asian Football Confederation's women's international player of the year award, completing a unique treble for the Australian forward.

The move disrupts the administration’s plan to confirm judges before Democrats take control of Congress, following a heated Senate exchange with Ted Cruz.

summary: A union representing political staff in New South Wales says employees are enduring unprecedented levels of violence, including spitting, swearing and death threats. The report highlights growing hostility towards staffers working for state politicians and calls for stronger protections.

summary: Neil Maxwell, the agent for Australian Test captain Pat Cummins, criticised the media frenzy surrounding the ongoing sandpaper controversy. He described the coverage as “hysteria” and urged focus on the facts as investigations continue.

summary: Former Liberal MP and ex-minister Sharman Stone, aged 75, died through voluntary assisted dying after a prolonged battle with glioblastoma. Stone had previously advocated for personal autonomy over medical decisions during her political career.

summary: Former US president Donald Trump revealed he bought shares in Nvidia, debt of SpaceX and Tesla stock in September, alongside other investments. The disclosures come as his ties to federal deals and the White House have intensified scrutiny.

headline: Canberra unveils new designs for City Hill park
summary: Draft concept designs for Canberra’s iconic City Hill park have been released, inviting public feedback on how the space could be used. The proposals aim to refresh the capital’s central green area with new amenities and landscaping.

summary: ABC readers shared how a recession-like environment is affecting them, from small business owners struggling with cash flow to mortgage holders feeling pressure from rising costs. The collection of stories highlights growing financial strain across the community.

summary: A continued shortage of Sanofi’s treatment for Pompe disease is causing patients to miss critical doses, raising concerns about health impacts. The supply issue persists, prompting worries among affected families and healthcare providers.
